last_amend_reason: ESC-013 approved class, tickets.json verify fields ONLY, 1 ticket. T-158 is repointed off apps/exchange/tests/test_repro_open_tickets.py -k test_t158_a_second_accept_on_a_reloaded_auction_record_mints_no_second_code and onto apps/exchange/tests/test_t158_acceptance_claim.py, the whole file. THE REASON IS NOT THAT THE OLD GATE WAS WEAK. It was SATISFIABLE IN THE WRONG DIRECTION, which is worse than a gate that cannot fail: it was green for the unsafe implementation and red for the correct one, so T-158 could only ever have been closed by making the system less safe. Measured on the old node body, 72 lines: 6 calls to accept(, and ZERO occurrences of TestClient, create_app, reserve, claim(, subprocess or Popen. It loads one auction twice from the store and calls accept() with no claim port injected, then names its own remedy - a process-wide in-memory AcceptLedger, citing the precedent at apps/buyer/svc/src/accept/handoff.py:187. That is exactly the fix the orchestrator rejected when briefing the lane, because an in-process ledger cannot tell process memory from durable state: it would turn that gate green while the cross-process double-spend stayed live. So the old gate rewarded the weaker fix and penalised the durable one, and that is why it still XFAILed after a working fix landed. Measured on the new file: 11 test functions, ZERO xfail markers, 11 passed, and it exercises what the ticket is actually about - 4 subprocess plus 1 Popen for a real OS process boundary (test_two_os_processes_accepting_one_auction_mint_exactly_one_code), 3 TestClient plus 3 create_app for the real served route (test_two_concurrent_accepts_through_the_served_route_mint_once), 26 uses of reserve for the atomic primitive including test_the_redis_store_reserves_atomically_across_independent_instances, thread races, and 8 uses of disarm for test_the_cross_process_harness_reproduces_the_double_spend_when_disarmed. That last one is the property that matters most: a disarm control means a green cannot come from a harness that never reproduces the defect in the first place. Worker slot carried forward verbatim as ${PROXYSHOP_GATE_WORKER:-2}. No --runxfail in the new command because the new file has no xfail markers - it is a live suite, not a repro gate. THE OLD NODE IS LEFT IN PLACE AND STILL CARRIES ITS STRICT XFAIL, so build_succeeds is unaffected (that file reads 13 passed, 7 xfailed, 0 failed) - but its docstring now names a WRONG remedy and is a trap for a future lane, and correcting that prose is dispatched separately as a test-file edit. T-158 STAYS OPEN on its rejected verdict until an independent verifier, already running, reproduces the exploit and confirms it is dead across a process boundary. Verified with the formatting-immune structural comparison rather than the line grep: zero tickets added, zero removed, fields changed = verify on T-158 only.
